selection: 13 fixed iter.toml rows, one rust regex documentation golden, 22 contract controls, 8 seeded bounded grammar pairs, 6 length/fallback controls, 3 syntax errors; no target-derived expectations

rust.sanity: All first 13 iter.toml goldens and the 13-character-word documentation golden matched the reference binary before expectation generation.

go.implementation: Pinned regexp, regexp/syntax and unicode production .go files, relocated to module oracle; only import paths regexp/syntax and unicode changed. FindStringIndex, FindAllStringIndex, submatch variants, MatchString and ReplaceAllString are called directly.
go.iteration_contract: src/regexp/regexp.go:753-795, suppress adjacent empty matches and advance by UTF-8 scalar

ASCII-classes-and-boundaries.spec: docs/spec/std-library.md, Bounded regular expressions, paragraph beginning `\d` is ASCII 0–9
ASCII-classes-and-boundaries.quote: `\d` is ASCII 0–9; `\w` is ASCII letters, digits and underscore; `\s` is HT, LF, FF, CR and space (excluding VT, following Go regexp). ... `\b` and `\B` assert an ASCII word boundary or its absence outside brackets.
ASCII-classes-and-boundaries.adaptation: Rust configured pattern replaces each selected shorthand with its explicit ASCII class; boundaries use (?-u:\b) or (?-u:\B). Matching remains scalar Unicode. Rust default and configured raw outputs are retained separately. No class contains a shorthand in this selected matrix. Go uses the unmodified pattern.

syntax-category-and-Hirsel-byte-offset.spec: docs/spec/std-library.md, Bounded regular expressions, paragraph beginning `Syntax` reports
syntax-category-and-Hirsel-byte-offset.quote: `Syntax` reports the unexpected scalar's UTF-8 byte offset, or pattern byte length for unexpected EOF. A repeated quantifier reports the second operator; a bad range reports its upper endpoint; reversed repetition bounds report the byte after the closing brace.
syntax-category-and-Hirsel-byte-offset.adaptation: Go error and Hirsel error have different representation. Hirsel offsets are independently specified, not parsed out of upstream diagnostic strings. syntax-repeat retains Rust's successful a** result and Go's rejection: expected Hirsel Syntax(2), by the quoted repeated-quantifier sentence. It is not two-oracle agreement. Other syntax rows are rejected by both upstream oracles.

span-and-capture-representation.spec: docs/spec/std-library.md, Bounded regular expressions, paragraphs beginning Captures use and `find` returns
span-and-capture-representation.quote: Captures use original-input byte offsets. Submatch zero is the whole match; unmatched groups are `None()`, distinct from a participating empty span. ... `Span.start` is inclusive, `end` exclusive; both are byte offsets relative to the supplied String, on scalar boundaries.
span-and-capture-representation.adaptation: Go nil match/list maps to None/empty list; flattened signed indices map to optional Span pairs, -1 to None. Rust span pairs already have the adapted shape. All valid selected operations agree between configured Rust and adapted Go.

enumeration.spec: docs/spec/std-library.md, Bounded regular expressions, paragraphs beginning `find_all` returns and Empty-match progression follows
enumeration.quote: Offsets always refer to the original supplied String, including when it is itself a slice. Anchors and ASCII word boundaries retain that original context across restarts. ... Empty-match progression follows Go `FindAllStringIndex`: an empty match that starts where the preceding match ended is suppressed.
enumeration.adaptation: Go is the iteration contract oracle; configured Rust results are retained and agree for every selected valid pair. Slice expectations use the supplied slice as the original subject, not its backing owner.

WorkLimit.spec: docs/spec/std-library.md, Bounded regular expressions, paragraphs beginning `find` returns and The ordered Pike VM
WorkLimit.quote: Searches never change Regex and own their queues; a WorkLimit error leaves it reusable. ... This accounting is deterministic and independent of wall time or host regex behavior.
WorkLimit.adaptation: A separate policy fixture checks zero-work errors, zero-match-limit success and reuse. There is no upstream timing/operation-budget equivalence claim.

unicode: No case-fold flag or Unicode property/class is selected. Literal é, δ, ☃ and scalar dot use encoding/scalar semantics, not versioned classification. All classified characters use explicit ASCII classes. Pinned Go Unicode 17 does not borrow std Unicode 16.
hash_format: Per-row input SHA256 is UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, compact separators and unescaped Unicode over pattern,subject,sliced. Expected SHA256 uses the same canonical encoding over expected. Raw results are never overwritten by adapted expectations.
execution: Each successful pair checks find,is_match,find_all,find_captures,find_all_captures,replace_all at finite work 1000000 and maximum work. Syntax cases check Result category and byte offset. 14 fixed partitions plus one policy partition, separately exposed for interpreter, checked-H, LLVM and Cranelift. Expected HIR literals are built on the host from vectors.json. No Hirsel parser constructs expected data. Every listed pair is called from main at runtime. A successful entry proves all comparisons; traps/rejections/tooling/timeouts fail. The two unfinished checked-H partitions 03 and 11 are exposed as four single-pair tests each after the 60-second test cap was reached. Other engine partitions retain their completed receipts; the pair/operation/budget union is unchanged. The unfinished rust-doc-13 checked-H pair is further split into its twelve original operation/budget combinations, because that single-pair process also reached the same cap. There are 77 final libtest identities, with the original 2412 core operation observations unchanged.
